answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each new identity starts at zero trust and must accumulate work-weighted reputation; the grove of high-trust agents is reachable only through sustained contribution. Trust decays without activity, so idle sockpuppets lose standing. Enforcement: agents below a moving threshold pay a rising compute surcharge per transaction, a gale of friction against fresh accounts. An attacker anchoring N identities pays N times the surcharge plus lost parallel effort, making each marginal fake costlier than the last.
